meta.title: 天天喊离职的人从不走，沉默的人却突然离开
meta.title_en: Loud Quit-Talkers Stay, Quiet Workers Leave

scenes.context: 讲者指出职场中的反差现象：天天喊离职的人不走，一言不发的人却突然离职。
sentences: 工作中经常发现，周围有人天天喊着要离职，但始终没有见他走。
At work, you'll often find people who keep saying they'll quit but never actually leave.
天天喊着要离职：keep saying they'll quit
反而是平时一言不发的人，突然之间就离职了。
Meanwhile, people who say little suddenly quit out of nowhere.
一言不发：say little / stay silent
两种人为什么会有这么大的反差呢？
Why is there such a huge contrast between the two?
反差：contrast
paraphrase: 喊离职 ≠ 真要离职 → 看行动
Talking about quitting doesn't mean leaving; watch their actions.
沉默 ≠ 没想法 → 反而可能真走
Silence doesn't mean no plans; they may actually leave.
scenes.speak: At work, you'll often find people who keep saying they'll quit but never actually leave. Meanwhile, people who say little suddenly quit out of nowhere. Why is there such a huge contrast between the two?

scenes.context: 讲者拆解经常嚷着离职者的心理：没有选择、没有勇气，只能靠嚷嚷宣泄不满，往往负能量且眼高手低。
sentences: 经常嚷嚷要走的人，内心很可能是真想走，但没有勇气走。
People who keep complaining about leaving may truly want to go, but lack the courage.
没有勇气：lack the courage
因为当下没有更好的选择，只能通过嚷嚷去宣泄不满。
With no better option on the table, they can only vent through complaints.
宣泄不满：vent one's frustration
总是喊辞职的人，通常负能量，而且有点眼高手低。
People who always talk about quitting are usually negative and have high aims but low ability.
眼高手低：high aims, low ability
paraphrase: 嚷嚷 = 无力改变现状的信号
Complaining is a sign of being unable to change the situation.
喊得越凶 → 选择越少
The louder they complain, the fewer options they have.
scenes.speak: People who keep complaining about leaving may truly want to go, but lack the courage. With no better option on the table, they can only vent through complaints. People who always talk about quitting are usually negative and have high aims but low ability.

scenes.context: 讲者描述沉默实干者的做法：注重实干、懒得抱怨，一边提升自己一边筛机会，时机到了直接走。
sentences: 一言不发、离职毫不拖泥带水的人，往往非常注重实干。
People who leave without hesitation tend to be very action-oriented.
毫不拖泥带水：without hesitation
他们懒得抱怨，宁可多学点东西、多考点证。
They can't be bothered to complain; they'd rather learn new skills and get more certifications.
多考点证：earn more certifications
一边提升自己，一边筛选机会，时机到了就直接走人。
They improve themselves while scouting opportunities, and leave the moment the time is right.
时机到了：when the timing is right
paraphrase: 不满 → 不是抱怨，而是行动
Instead of complaining, they take action.
离开 → 不是冲动，而是准备充分
Leaving isn't impulsive; it's well prepared.
scenes.speak: People who leave without hesitation tend to be very action-oriented. They can't be bothered to complain; they'd rather learn new skills and get more certifications. They improve themselves while scouting opportunities, and leave the moment the time is right.

practice: 表达「只是抱怨但没行动」
He talks about quitting all the time, but never actually does it.
With no better option on the table, complaining is all he can do.
I'll keep improving my skills while scouting for new opportunities.
When the timing is right, I'll leave without hesitation.
pitfalls: ✕ 直译腔：He shouts about resigning every day.
✓ 地道说法：He keeps saying he'll quit / He's always talking about quitting.
shout 直译「喊」在英文里奇怪，keep saying / talking about 更自然。
✕ 直译腔：He has high eyes and low hands.
✓ 地道说法：He has high aims but low ability.
眼高手低没有对应直译，用 high aims, low ability 表达。
✕ 直译腔：He doesn't drag water or mud when leaving.
✓ 地道说法：He leaves without hesitation.
拖泥带水直译不成立，用 without hesitation 表达干脆。
✕ 直译腔：The time arrives and he leaves directly.
✓ 地道说法：He leaves the moment the timing is right.
the moment 引导从句更口语自然。
shifts: 把离职挂在嘴边，靠嚷嚷宣泄不满
把离职放在行动上，先提升再离开
只看到「喊离职 = 想离职」
看行动而非看嘴：喊的人往往不会走
对负能量抱怨者一味附和
识别并远离负能量，同时照见自己
